caution: A failure to reproduce is not a finding that the paper is wrong. It may be a failure of the attempt.

attempts.label: CRCNS:ssc-8
attempts.entry_title: Network synchrony in the developing barrel cortex of Fmr1 knockout mice (Goncalves et al. 2013)
attempts.summary: The paper's calcium imaging findings held up in part in this data; its whole-cell, EEG and anesthesia findings could not be tested, as those recordings are not deposited. Correlation between nearby neurons fell with age in both genotypes and, pooled over ages, was higher in Fmr1 knockout mice, though the pooled means missed the paper's values. The genotype difference at P14-16, which the paper calls largest, missed significance (p = 0.057), and the larger share of knockout neurons joining peaks of synchrony was not found. The paper does not fully define these measures, and the deposited groups differ in size from its sample. Firing rates did not differ between genotypes, as reported.
attempts.description: Tests the calcium imaging findings of Goncalves, Anstey, Golshani and Portera-Cailliau (2013) on CRCNS data set ssc-8, which holds the estimated firing rates and cell-to-cell distances of L2/3 barrel cortex neurons in unanesthetized WT and Fmr1 knockout mice at three ages. It compares pairwise correlation between genotypes and ages, peaks of synchrony and firing rates. The whole-cell, EEG, isoflurane and 15.6 Hz data of the paper are not in the data set.

notebooks.title: Reproducing Goncalves et al. (2013) from CRCNS ssc-8

outcomes.statement: The calcium imaging of unanesthetized mice comprises 12, 9 and 8 WT mice and 9, 10 and 8 Fmr1 -/- mice at P9-11, P14-16 and P30-40.
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical network synchrony is high in Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 1; Fig. 1e
outcomes.quote: n = 12, 9, 8 WT mice at P9-11, P14-16, and P30-40, respectively and n = 9, 10, 8 Fmr1 –/– mice at the same ages, respectively
outcomes.notes: The MAT file and the TIFF archive agree on 13, 8 and 7 WT and 9, 10 and 6 KO mice at P9-11, P14-16 and P30-40 (28 WT and 25 KO), against 12, 9, 8 and 9, 10, 8 in Fig. 1e (29 and 27). Two of six groups match (KO P9-11 and KO P14-16). The P14-16 counts (8 WT, 10 KO) match neither the Fig. 1e counts nor the reversed n of the peaks of synchrony sentence (10 WT, 9 KO). No recording is deposited twice (no identical movie or cell trace).

outcomes.statement: In WT mice, the drop in pairwise correlation from P9-11 (12 mice) to P14-16 (9 mice) is largest for cells less than 100 um apart (mean difference 0.223) and smaller for cells 100-200 um (0.159) and more than 200 um apart (0.067, not significant).
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical network synchrony is high in Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 1; Fig. 1d
outcomes.quote: cell pairs located within 100 µm of one another displayed the largest differences in pair-wise correlation coefficients between P9-11 (n = 12 mice) and P14-16 (n = 9 mice), compared to cells farther apart (mean difference 0.223, p<0.0001 for cells <100 μm apart, 0.159, p<0.0001 for cells 100-200 μm apart and 0.067, p=0.0598 for cells >200 μm apart; two-way ANOVA with Bonferroni corrected p values

statistics.about: P9-11 against P14-16, pairs under 100 um
statistics.test: two-way ANOVA, Bonferroni corrected post hoc
two-way ANOVA, Bonferroni corrected post hoc

statistics.about: P9-11 against P14-16, pairs over 200 um
statistics.test: two-way ANOVA, Bonferroni corrected post hoc

outcomes.notes: WT mice, 13 at P9-11 and 8 at P14-16. Under the main reading (C-b, zero-lag normalised cross-correlation of the estimated rates) the P9-11 minus P14-16 difference is 0.191 under 100 um, 0.105 at 100 to 200 um and 0.025 over 200 um, against 0.223, 0.159 and 0.067. The Bonferroni corrected p are 6.6e-08, 0.0019 and 1.0 under A-a and 2.4e-05, 0.0066 and 1.0 under A-b, so the significance pattern holds, and the difference falls with distance; none of the three differences is within the 10% tolerance. The Spearman variant gives 0.175, 0.108 and 0.051. Only 4 of 8 P14-16 mice and 12 of 13 P9-11 mice have pairs over 200 um; on the mice with all three bins the differences are 0.188, 0.102 and 0.025, with within-bin Bonferroni p of 0.0012, 0.022 and 1. The four P14-16 mice with pairs over 200 um have 28, 108, 72 and 1 such pairs, so the third bin rests partly on four mice.
deviations: The data set holds 13 and 8 WT mice at these ages, not 12 and 9.

The trace is the deposited estimated firing rate (reading T-a). Reading T-b, the low-pass filtered dF/F, cannot be run, as the data set holds no cell contours or dF/F traces; the outcome is assumed to hold for the trace the paper used. The Methods say only "pair-wise continuous-trace cross-correlations as previously described 15".

The post hoc test of A-a uses the two-way ANOVA's pooled residual mean square; that of A-b is a t-test within each bin, both with Bonferroni over three bins. The text does not give the form. The A-b post hoc uses every mouse with pairs in a bin, while the split-plot ANOVA uses the 16 mice with all three bins; on those 16 mice the post hoc gives the same pattern.

outcomes.statement: For cell pairs within 100 um, correlation decreases significantly with age in both WT and Fmr1 -/- mice.
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical network synchrony is high in Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 1; Fig. 1e
outcomes.quote: When we quantified pairwise correlation coefficients for cells within 100 μm, we found a statistically significant age-dependent decrease in network synchrony for both WT and Fmr1 –/– mice (two-way unequal variance ANOVA, p<0.01 for both genotypes
outcomes.notes: Pairs under 100 um, reading C-b. WT 0.360, 0.169 and 0.119 at the three ages (13, 8, 7 mice), KO 0.421, 0.204 and 0.134 (9, 10, 6 mice). The 2-df age contrast within genotype of the unequal-variance model gives F = 52.5 (df2 14.9, p = 1.8e-07) for WT and F = 64.3 (df2 14.1, p = 8.1e-08) for KO. Welch's one-way ANOVA gives the same numbers, as the Welch-James test reduces to it for a one-way design, so readings E-a and E-b agree. The Spearman variant agrees.
deviations: Group sizes differ from the paper's (see group-sizes).

outcomes.statement: Pooling all ages, correlation coefficients are higher in Fmr1 -/- than WT mice (0.265 +/- 0.009 against 0.230 +/- 0.008, p = 0.0057).
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical network synchrony is high in Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 1; Fig. 1e
outcomes.quote: we found significantly higher correlation coefficients for cell pairs in Fmr1 –/– mice when pooling data for all ages (average corr. coefficient 0.230 ± 0.008 for WT vs. 0.265 ± 0.009 for Fmr1 –/– , p = 0.0057, two-way unequal variance ANOVA)
outcomes.notes: The genotype main effect of the unequal-variance 2 x 3 model is significant with KO higher, p = 0.0064 (F = 8.48, df2 33.5) for pairs under 100 um and p = 0.0028 for all pairs (paper 0.0057). No reading puts both means within the paper's s.e.m. Under 100 um over all mice (P-a, M-a, given as measured) WT 0.245 and KO 0.265, KO within and WT not; all pairs over mice (P-b, M-a) WT 0.223 and KO 0.251, WT within and KO not; mean of the age means (M-b) WT 0.216 and KO 0.253 under 100 um, 0.198 and 0.240 for all pairs. The s.e.m. under M-b (0.0088 and 0.0093) is close to the paper's (0.008 and 0.009), while that over mice is 0.024 and 0.026, which points to M-b, the equal-weight average of the age means, as the paper's form; under M-b both means are about 0.013 below the paper's, outside tolerance, which supports the partial outcome.
deviations: Group sizes differ from the paper's (see group-sizes), which moves the pooled means.
The trace is the estimated firing rate (T-a); T-b cannot be run (see fig1d-distance-dependent-decorrelation). The outcome is assumed to hold for the paper's trace.

The unequal-variance ANOVA is fitted on the six cell means with their variances of the mean, and the genotype contrast tested with the Welch-James statistic and Satterthwaite degrees of freedom; the claims file names this standard choice.

outcomes.statement: With Pearson correlation, pooled over ages, coefficients are again higher in Fmr1 -/- than WT mice (0.196 +/- 0.010 against 0.164 +/- 0.009, p = 0.026).
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical network synchrony is high in Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 1; Suppl. Fig. 1 (not in the text read)
outcomes.quote: Similar results were found when we calculated correlation coefficients using the Pearson method (average corr. coefficient 0.164 ± 0.009 for WT vs. 0.196 ± 0.010 for Fmr1 –/– , p = 0.026, two-way unequal-variance ANOVA

statistics.about: genotype main effect, all ages, Pearson

outcomes.notes: Pearson correlation. The genotype effect is significant with KO higher, p = 0.023 for pairs under 100 um (paper 0.026) and 0.012 for all pairs. No reading puts both means within the paper's s.e.m. Under 100 um over mice (given as measured) WT 0.179 and KO 0.193, KO within; all pairs over mice WT 0.155 and KO 0.178, WT within; means of the age means WT 0.146 and KO 0.180, with s.e.m. 0.0092 and 0.0107 against the paper's 0.009 and 0.010, which points to M-b as the paper's form; under it both means are below the paper's (by 0.018 and 0.016), outside tolerance.
deviations: Group sizes differ from the paper's; the trace is the estimated firing rate (T-a), and T-b cannot be run; the outcome is assumed to hold for the paper's trace.

outcomes.statement: The genotype difference is largest at P14-16, where correlation is 0.210 +/- 0.011 in Fmr1 -/- against 0.172 +/- 0.012 in WT mice (p = 0.032).
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical network synchrony is high in Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 1; Fig. 1e and 1f
outcomes.quote: The difference in correlation coefficients was most pronounced at P14-16 (0.172 ± 0.012 for WT vs. 0.210 ± 0.011 for Fmr1 –/– , p=0.032, t-test
outcomes.notes: At P14-16 the means are within the paper's s.e.m. (WT 0.169 +/- 0.010, 8 mice; KO 0.204 +/- 0.013, 10 mice) and KO is higher, but the unpaired Student's t-test gives t = 2.05, p = 0.057 (Welch's test, not the Methods' test, gives p = 0.049). The KO minus WT difference is 0.062 at P9-11, 0.035 at P14-16 and 0.015 at P30-40, so it is not largest at P14-16; as a ratio, a variant the criterion does not use, it is largest there (1.21 against 1.17 and 1.13). The Spearman variant gives p = 0.058. The variances do not differ (s.d. 0.029 and 0.040, Levene p = 0.31, Bartlett p = 0.39, F-test p = 0.40), so the Methods' check of variances leads to Student's test. The outcome is fragile. With one mouse left out in turn, Student p runs from 0.018 to 0.109 and is below 0.05 in 1 of 8 WT and 3 of 10 KO cases; leaving out the WT mouse of highest correlation (0.228) gives 0.018. The data set has one WT mouse fewer at P14-16 than the paper, so the difference in sample alone could move the test across 0.05.
deviations: The trace is the estimated firing rate (T-a); T-b cannot be run; the outcome is assumed to hold for the paper's trace.

outcomes.statement: By P30-40 the genotype difference in correlation has decreased and is not significant (0.144 +/- 0.008 in Fmr1 -/- against 0.123 +/- 0.008 in WT, p = 0.075).
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical network synchrony is high in Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 1; Fig. 1e
outcomes.quote: By P30-40, this difference in correlation coefficients in mice of both genotypes had decreased (0.144 ± 0.008 vs. 0.123 ± 0.008 for Fmr1 –/– and WT respectively, p = 0.075, t-test)
outcomes.notes: KO 0.134 +/- 0.011 (6 mice) against WT 0.119 +/- 0.005 (7 mice), difference 0.015, Student p = 0.22 (Welch 0.25), reading C-b. WT is within the paper's s.e.m. (0.123 +/- 0.008); KO is below it (0.144 +/- 0.008). The Spearman variant gives p = 0.62.
deviations: 6 KO and 7 WT mice, not 8 and 8.

outcomes.statement: The frequency of peaks of synchrony at P14-16 is slightly but not significantly higher in Fmr1 -/- mice (0.060 +/- 0.007 against 0.053 +/- 0.006 peaks per s, p = 0.45).
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical network synchrony is high in Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 2; Fig. 2b
outcomes.quote: The frequency of peaks of synchrony was slightly higher in Fmr1 –/– mice at P14-16, but the difference was not significant (0.060 ± 0.007 vs. 0.053 ± 0.006 peaks per s for Fmr1 –/– and WT, n = 9 and 10 mice, respectively; p=0.45; t-test

statistics.n: 9 Fmr1 -/- and 10 WT mice, as printed

outcomes.notes: P14-16, 10 KO and 8 WT mice. No reading finds a difference (p = 0.13 to 0.96). Under R-a (active when the rate is above 0) both means are within the paper's s.e.m. with either shuffle; with S-a (given as measured) KO 0.060 +/- 0.006 and WT 0.054 +/- 0.007 peaks per s, p = 0.52; with S-b 0.061 and 0.057, p = 0.64. Under R-b (at least one estimated spike in the frame) with the rates in Hz (rate / 3.9 >= 1) events are rarer, 0.016 to 0.027 per s, outside the tolerances, p = 0.13 and 0.45. Under R-b with the rates per frame (rate >= 1, met by 97% of non-zero values) KO 0.055 and WT 0.053 with S-a (p = 0.82), and 0.059 and 0.059 with S-b (p = 0.96). Thresholds under R-a are 23 to 37.5% of cells active. At 4 Hz the frequencies rise by 2.6% and the tests do not change.
deviations: 8 WT mice, against 10 in the text (and 9 in Fig. 1e).

The definition of an active cell and the shuffle are not given in the paper; the claims file's readings were run, with R-b under both rate units (six readings), and give the same outcome. The shuffle seeds are a standard choice.

outcomes.statement: At P14-16 a higher proportion of neurons participates in peaks of synchrony in Fmr1 -/- than in WT mice (0.380 +/- 0.023 against 0.300 +/- 0.017, p = 0.023).
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical network synchrony is high in Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 2; Fig. 2c
outcomes.quote: However the proportion of neurons that participated in peaks of synchrony was significantly higher in Fmr1 –/– mice than in WT mice at P14-16 (0.380 ± 0.023 vs. 0.300 ± 0.017 for Fmr1 –/– and WT respectively; p = 0.023; t-test
outcomes.notes: No reading gives a significant genotype difference (p = 0.052 to 0.76 over twelve readings). Under R-a, S-a and Q-a (given as measured) KO 0.444 +/- 0.020 and WT 0.411 +/- 0.019, p = 0.25; both are above the paper's 0.380 and 0.300. Under R-a nearly every cell joins at least one event (Q-b 0.998 to 1.0). Under R-b Q-a is 0.17 against 0.13 to 0.14 and Q-b 0.66 against 0.49 to 0.54, KO higher, p = 0.15 to 0.37. Under R-b with the rates per frame (rate >= 1) Q-a is KO 0.437 against WT 0.391 with S-a (p = 0.052) and 0.429 against 0.385 with S-b (p = 0.053), KO higher and near significance, both outside tolerance; Q-b is 0.998 in both (p = 0.76). No mouse lacks events. As that p sits at 0.05 and the threshold comes from 100 seeded shuffles, the reading was run with 20 further seeds per shuffle. With S-a p is 0.056 to 0.116 (median 0.069), below 0.05 in none of 20; with S-b p is 0.044 to 0.116 (median 0.060), below 0.05 with KO higher in 3 of 20. With 1000 shuffles per threshold p is 0.056 (S-a) and 0.051 to 0.054 (S-b, three seeds). The typical draw and the limit of the Methods' procedure do not reach p < 0.05; the outcome is close to the boundary. In every draw both means are outside tolerance (KO 0.426 to 0.436, WT 0.383 to 0.397), so where the test holds the outcome would be partially reproduced.
deviations: 8 WT mice at P14-16, not 9 or 10.

The definition of the proportion, of an active cell and of the shuffle are not given in the paper; the claims file's readings were run, with R-b under both rate units (twelve readings), and give the same outcome. The threshold uses 100 shuffles (Online Methods, network events); the seed check in the notes shows how much its sampling noise moves the closest reading.

outcomes.statement: Firing rates extrapolated from the calcium imaging by deconvolution do not differ between genotypes at any age.
outcomes.source: Results, Cortical network synchrony is high in Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 2 (data not shown)
outcomes.quote: we calculated neuronal firing rates, as extrapolated from calcium imaging data by temporal deconvolution (see Methods), but could not detect differences between genotypes at any age using this method (not shown)
outcomes.notes: KO minus WT is 0.017 Hz at P9-11 (0.446 against 0.429, p = 0.73), 0.0002 Hz at P14-16 (0.304 against 0.304, p = 0.997) and 0.014 Hz at P30-40 (0.371 against 0.356, p = 0.76). Reading the rates as per frame scales both groups by 3.9 and does not change the tests.
deviations: Group sizes differ from the paper's (see group-sizes).

outcomes.statement: In unanesthetized P14-16 mice the extrapolated firing rate is 0.30 +/- 0.03 Hz in WT and 0.29 +/- 0.03 Hz in Fmr1 -/- mice, and the correlation of pairs within 100 um is 0.17 +/- 0.01 in WT mice.
outcomes.source: Results, Network activity is unchanged by anesthesia in mutant mice, paragraphs 1 and 2; Fig. 6
outcomes.quote: significantly higher in isoflurane-anesthetized WT mice than in unanesthetized WT mice (0.24 ± 0.02 vs. 0.17 ± 0.01, n = 9 and 9 mice ... isoflurane had a significant effect on extrapolated firing rates of L2/3 neurons in WT mice (0.30 ± 0.03 vs. 0.21 ± 0.02 Hz for unanesthetized and isoflurane, respectively ... but did not change neuronal firing in Fmr1 –/– mice (0.29± 0.03 vs. 0.27 ± 0.02 Hz for unanesthetized and isoflurane, respectively
outcomes.notes: With the rates read as Hz (U-a), WT 0.304 +/- 0.027 Hz (8 mice) and KO 0.304 +/- 0.027 Hz (10 mice), within 0.30 +/- 0.03 and 0.29 +/- 0.03; the WT correlation of pairs under 100 um is 0.169 +/- 0.010 (C-b), within 0.17 +/- 0.01. Read as per frame (U-b) the rates would be 1.19 Hz. The data descriptor gives no unit. The values are 0 in about 90% of frames and average 0.19 to 0.74 per recording, which fits Hz, but this rests on the means lying near the paper's values, which are the values tested, and is partly circular. The values themselves do not show the unit; they are continuous (1.06 million distinct values among 1.18 million non-zero ones) and fall within 0.01 of a multiple of 1 or of 3.9 no more often than continuous values would (0.020 against 0.020, 0.0043 against 0.0051). The criterion accepts one reading of rate unit.
deviations: The unanesthetized groups of Fig. 6 are taken to be the P14-16 mice of Fig. 1e, as the claims file reads them; the data set has 8 WT, not 9.

outcomes.statement: In whole-cell recordings at P14-16, L2/3 neurons of Fmr1 -/- mice fire 3-fold more than WT neurons during Up/Down states (0.40 +/- 0.05 Hz against 0.13 +/- 0.04 Hz).
outcomes.source: Results, High firing rates during Up/Down states Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 1; Fig. 3e
outcomes.quote: We discovered that L2/3 neurons in Fmr1 –/– mice had 3-fold higher firing rates than WT mice during Up-Down states (0.40 ± 0.05 Hz, n = 6 recordings from 6 cells in 4 mice vs. 0.13 ± 0.04 Hz, n = 5 recordings from 5 cells in 5 mice; Bonferroni corrected p = 0.040, 2-way ANOVA

statistics.n: 6 Fmr1 -/- recordings (6 cells, 4 mice) and 5 WT recordings (5 cells, 5 mice)

outcomes.notes: The data set holds only calcium imaging (the bucket's ssc-8/live/ lists the TIFF archive, the MAT file of rates and distances, and the descriptor). The descriptor and the paper name no deposit of the whole-cell recordings.

outcomes.statement: In whole-cell recordings, WT neurons tend to fire more in FOA (0.290 +/- 0.158 Hz) than in Up/Down segments (0.133 +/- 0.036 Hz), but not significantly; Fmr1 -/- neurons show the opposite tendency, for which the paper gives no values or test.
outcomes.source: Results, High firing rates during Up/Down states Fmr1 -/- mice, paragraph 1; Fig. 3e

There was also an opposite trend for Fmr1 –/– mice, which showed a tendency toward higher firing rates during Up/Down states compared to FOA

outcomes.notes: The claim needs no EEG, but its sample is the 3-min recordings of the EEG subset (13 WT and 10 KO), which the data set does not identify; it holds one concatenated recording per mouse and does not mark which recordings, if any, were in the subset. Whether those recordings are deposited at all is unknown, so data_missing may apply as well. As a variant that decides nothing, the P14-16 recordings of exactly 2160 frames (4 WT and 6 KO mice) cut into three 720-frame segments give KO r2 = 0.216 (slope positive, p = 0.052, 18 segments) and WT r2 = 0.116 (p = 0.28, 12 segments); segments of one mouse are not independent. In each recording used the median brightness step at frames 720 and 1440 is above the median step (ratio 1.08 to 13.5).

findings.statement: The data set holds 13, 8 and 7 WT mice and 9, 10 and 6 Fmr1 -/- mice at P9-11, P14-16 and P30-40 (53), while the paper analysed 12, 9 and 8 and 9, 10 and 8 (56). Neither the descriptor nor the files say which mice differ from the paper's sample or why.

The descriptor gives 40 to 149 neurons per animal; two WT P9-11 recordings have 164 and 198. It gives about 7 to 8 min per recording; at the stated 3.9 Hz the recordings last 3.8 to 15.4 min, and 27 of 53 are 2160 frames (9.2 min).

The descriptor gives no unit for the estimated firing rates; their means fit Hz, and the values, which are continuous, do not show the unit. It does not say that the k-th matrix of each group belongs to Movie_k.tif, which the frame counts and the correlation of the population rate with each movie's brightness show.

The movie folders are named "4Hz" where the paper and the descriptor give 3.9 Hz, and most recordings are 2160 frames, three 3-min movies at 4 Hz. Frames are 128 x 256 pixels in 50 movies (and 357, 404 and 512 wide in one each), where the Methods give 512 x 128. The TIFFs carry no time stamps, so the frame rate cannot be checked.

No cell contours or dF/F traces are deposited, so the paper's correlations cannot be computed from the filtered dF/F if that is what the paper used; only the estimated firing rates are given. The whole-cell recordings, the EEG, the isoflurane imaging and the 15.6 Hz imaging are not deposited, and 17 of the paper's 28 claims cannot be tested.
The TIFF archive holds five macOS resource-fork files (._.DS_Store and ._Movie_1.tif) beside the 53 movies.

Question for the authors. Which trace and which measure give the pairwise correlation of Fig. 1 (the Methods refer to ref. 15 for "continuous-trace cross-correlations")? Was it the deconvolved trace deposited here or the filtered dF/F, was the mean subtracted, and at which lag? The zero-lag normalised cross-correlation of the deposited rates gives the paper's P14-16 values (WT 0.169, KO 0.204) but pooled means that differ from the paper's.

Question for the authors. For peaks of synchrony, when is a cell active in a frame, how was each trace shuffled, and how is the proportion of neurons participating in an event formed? With an active cell as any non-zero rate the frequencies match the paper's, but no reading gives proportions within the paper's s.e.m. (0.300 and 0.380). Q-a with R-b and the rates in Hz gives proportions below them (0.13 to 0.17), and every other reading gives proportions above them.

Question for the authors. How was the pooled average correlation (0.230 and 0.265) formed, and how was the unequal-variance 2 x 3 ANOVA fitted? The paper's s.e.m. fit an average of the three age means, not the mean over mice.

entries.name: goncalves-2013
entries.title: Network synchrony in the developing barrel cortex of Fmr1 knockout mice (Goncalves et al. 2013)
entries.description: Tests the calcium imaging findings of Goncalves, Anstey, Golshani and Portera-Cailliau (2013) on CRCNS data set ssc-8, which holds the estimated firing rates and cell-to-cell distances of L2/3 barrel cortex neurons in unanesthetized WT and Fmr1 knockout mice at three ages. It compares pairwise correlation between genotypes and ages, peaks of synchrony and firing rates. The whole-cell, EEG, isoflurane and 15.6 Hz data of the paper are not in the data set.
